title: What 20 years of NSE data say
data: Daily closes Oct 2006 – Oct 2026, 1,712 stocks listed on NSE today, 59,125 first breakouts from bases of 25+ days with ₹1 Cr+ daily turnover and a full year of data after. Returns are 1-year excess over NIFTY 500 from the breakout close; 'Failed' = closed 5%+ back inside the base within 20 sessions; 'Doubled' = rose 100%+ at some point within the year.
findings: Base length on its own does not predict a bigger move. Across all breakouts, long and short bases did about the same, and the 'longer the base' effect disappears once trend, RS and tightness are accounted for.

Long bases do pay when the stock is already in an uptrend: above a rising 150-day and the 200-day average with RS 70+. There, 200–399-day bases beat NIFTY 500 by about 20% on average over the next year, against about 11% for 25–49-day bases, and more than half beat the index. 400–799 days was next best; 800+ days (3+ years) was no better than short bases.

Outside an uptrend, long bases gave no edge: every length bucket beat NIFTY 500 by only about 1–6% on average and fewer than half beat it at all, and bases of 400+ days were the weakest — a long base under a falling average is usually a stock that is still weak.

RS at the breakout was the most reliable single factor in both halves of the period. A tight right side (last 15 sessions within 6–9%) cut failures by about a third. Bases the stock built after an advance did better than ranges it fell into after a decline.
Very heavy breakout volume did not help on average (Bulkowski found the same), so volume is shown but not scored.
The Base Score combines these. Its bands lined up in order in 2007–16 and again in 2017–26: from about +3% a year over NIFTY 500 under 40 to about +17% at 80+, with failures falling from 39% to 32%.
caveats: Only stocks still listed today (companies that were delisted are missing, which flatters all returns a little, but affects every bucket). Averages are trimmed at the 0.5% tails. Past results are evidence, not a promise.
